episode.acceptanceBasis: site deployed to production and retained unchanged; user confirmed satisfaction out of band. Terminal acceptance is tacit — retention without further correction is the acceptance signal (Demonstrated Preference).

correctionLoops.discoveredSpec: Pixelated in appearance, continuous in motion: parallax via sub-pixel CSS transform (never stepping the shader grid), stars twinkle in place, randomness visually uncorrelated (CPU-generated texture, not GPU float hash), field regenerates on a slow ~6s epoch.

correctionLoops.theme: Constellation placement, scale, and layering (mobile + desktop)
correctionLoops.discoveredSpec: Constellation as its own layer above the starfield, out of the shader; desktop keeps the originally-accepted upper-right composition; mobile hero is sky-only with a uniform-scale dipper; background stars begin below a noise-roughened diagonal so the constellation's corner stays clean; constellation follows the pointer.

Darkness needs headroom: top-of-page ambience bright enough that scroll darkening (floor 0.35) reads as a real change; corners never pitch black (nebula floor ~0.12). 'Darker' was a direction, not a destination — the preference was contrast, not absolute darkness.
Deletion requests are content-scoped, never style-scoped: removing text the user dislikes must not remove typography the user loves. Edit boundaries must be minimal and explicit.

feedbackTranslations.complaint: i wish the background movement was smoother, and centered on the mouse. not opposite and away. its quite unsatisfying
feedbackTranslations.mechanism: Parallax was applied inside the shader on the pixel grid, so motion stepped in whole pixels (and direction was inverted). Fix: sub-pixel CSS transform on the canvas — continuous kinematics under a pixelated look.

feedbackTranslations.complaint: i know its supposed to be pixely, but right now it just looks like its crashing
feedbackTranslations.mechanism: Hash cells re-randomized as parallax shifted their coordinates, reading as flicker/shimmer; plus correlated GPU float-hash artifacts.

feedbackTranslations.complaint: the stars still look like diagonal lines. not randomly placed
feedbackTranslations.mechanism: Float-precision aliasing in the sin/fract GPU hash produced spatially correlated star placement. Interim fix: better hash (step 577, partial). Definitive: randomness moved to a CPU-filled RGBA texture sampled by the shader.

feedbackTranslations.complaint: its scaled too big and the text covers it, and it overlaps with frontier labs
feedbackTranslations.mechanism: Constellation scaled per-axis with the viewport, distorting the dipper's shape on portrait aspect ratios and colliding with DOM text the shader could not see. Fix path: uniform scaling, then DOM band measurement, finally extraction to its own layer.

feedbackTranslations.complaint: not really, its so dark overall i dont see changes upon scroll
feedbackTranslations.mechanism: Scroll darkening lacked contrast headroom — the page started too dark for a 0.42 floor to read as change. Fix inverted the approach: raise top-of-page ambience and deepen the floor to 0.35.

notes: All `step` values are assistant-step ordinals joinable to generations[].turnIndex and conversations[].prompts[].step; every labeled claim is auditable against the raw generation text and the user's verbatim prompt.

Correction loops cluster where language runs out (motion, placement, perceptual calibration); one-shots cluster where specs are stateable. The recurrence map locates where outcome-based signal replaces unavailable elicited preference.
Repair attempts are graded by the artifact (edit survival), not by a rater: wrong-diagnosis edits die at 0%, correct-diagnosis edits survive at 70–100%.

v1 labels are human-curated from the embedded prompt stream and generation churn; auto-detection heuristics (prompt clustering + same-file regeneration bursts; accepted-span disappearance for regressions) are specified in trajectory.md.
